solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: End of trendy red wine

parts.note: trendy means in, as in fashionable
tent is a deep red Spanish wine, once used as communion wine

explanation.surface: Someone ordering the last of a fashionable red wine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'End' looks like a pointer to a last letter, but it is the definition in its sense of purpose or aim.
explanation.definitionFit: An end in the sense of a goal or purpose is a synonym of an aim or design.

clue.text: Standard supporter most of the time

parts.note: a standard is a norm
a supporter is an ally

explanation.surface: A regular backer who is around for most of the time.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing something as a rule, usually, is doing it most of the time: an idiomatic equivalent.

clue.text: Raised tax in English city in the north, not south

indicators.note: in places the tax inside the letters for English and the trimmed city
not tells us to drop the letter for south from the city name

parts.note: Leeds is a city in the north of England
VAT is value added tax

explanation.surface: A tax hike imposed on a northern English city but spared in the south.
explanation.walkthrough: 'English city' tempts you to take one word for both; English gives its own letter, and 'in the north' merely describes the city.
explanation.definitionFit: Something raised is lifted up to a higher level: a straightforward synonym.

clue.text: Almost swing over atrium, half- splitting wrist bone

indicators.note: in a down clue, over puts the first piece above the second
almost says the word for swing loses its final letter

parts.note: a trapeze is an acrobat's swing

indicators.note: splitting the word atrium in half and keeping its second half

explanation.surface: A trapeze artist swinging over a hotel atrium and breaking a wrist.
explanation.walkthrough: The stray hyphen in 'half- splitting' is as printed: read it as splitting the word in half and keeping the back part.
explanation.definitionFit: The trapezium is one of the eight small carpal bones of the human wrist.

clue.text: Muscle put on by corrupt copper on retirement

parts.note: to put on is to add

indicators.note: retirement is a going back, so the phrase corrupt copper is read backwards

parts.note: to corrupt is to rot
Cu is the chemical symbol for copper

explanation.surface: A bent policeman who has bulked up after leaving the force.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on retirement' turns ROTCU into UCTOR, which follows ADD.
explanation.definitionFit: An adductor is a muscle that draws a limb towards the body's midline.

clue.text: Unnamed adorable drunk that's a long way away

indicators.note: drunk suggests the letters are reeling into a new order

explanation.surface: An anonymous charming drunk who has wandered off a long way.
explanation.definitionFit: The Andromeda galaxy, once called a nebula, lies about two and a half million light years off: very distant indeed.

clue.text: Shadow over extremely grave offence

indicators.note: in a down clue, over sets the first piece above the second

parts.note: an umbra is the darkest part of a shadow

indicators.note: extremely asks for the extreme letters, first and last, of grave

explanation.surface: A shadow hanging over a very serious offence.
explanation.definitionFit: To take umbrage is to take offence, so the word is a synonym of resentment or offence.

clue.text: Foreign stadium initially to host, say, Eurovision legends

indicators.note: initially asks for the first letters of the words to and host

parts.note: say gives eg, for example
ABBA won the Eurovision Song Contest in 1974 with Waterloo

explanation.surface: An overseas stadium about to host a concert by famous Eurovision winners.
explanation.definitionFit: The Gabba is the nickname of the Brisbane Cricket Ground in Australia, a stadium abroad to a British setter.

clue.text: What's left dies horribly with you, ultimately in odd surroundings

indicators.note: in places the middle pieces within the word for odd
surroundings says the odd word wraps around the rest

parts.note: odd means rum, peculiar

indicators.note: horribly signals the letters of dies being mangled
ultimately takes the last letter of you

explanation.surface: Someone dying horribly in strange surroundings, and what remains afterwards.
explanation.walkthrough: 'odd' is not an alternate-letters signal here; it is a synonym, peculiar, forming the surroundings.
explanation.definitionFit: A residuum is the remainder or residue left after a process.

clue.text: Release control made without using mechnical devices

parts.note: to release is to free
hand as in having a hand in, control over something

explanation.surface: Letting go of the controls on something built without machinery.
explanation.definitionFit: A drawing done by hand alone, without rulers or other instruments, is made without any mechanical aids.

clue.text: Fat heartless swines emptied haunt

indicators.note: heartless removes the central letter of the word for fat

parts.note: fat means obese

indicators.note: emptied clears out the inside of swines, leaving its outer letters

explanation.surface: Plump, unfeeling pigs leaving an old hangout empty.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heartless' takes the middle E from OBESE, giving OBSE; 'emptied' leaves SS.
explanation.definitionFit: To haunt someone's thoughts is to preoccupy them constantly: a synonym in the verb sense.

clue.text: Short bird with single mate knocked back some hot stuff

indicators.note: short cuts the last letter from the bird's name

parts.note: a jay is a bird of the crow family

indicators.note: knocked back reads single mate in reverse order

parts.note: single means one
a mate is a pal

explanation.surface: A short bird and its only partner downing something fiery.
explanation.walkthrough: 'knocked back' turns ONEPAL into LAPENO, after JA.
explanation.definitionFit: The jalapeño is a fiery chilli pepper, so a fine example of hot stuff.

clue.text: South Africa entered into tough venture

indicators.note: entered into puts the country's code inside the word for tough

parts.note: tough means hard
ZA is the international code for South Africa

explanation.surface: South Africa signing up to a difficult undertaking.
explanation.definitionFit: To venture a guess is to risk it, the verb sense of chance or gamble.

clue.text: Testimony of retiring editor stopping show

indicators.note: stopping means plugging the gap inside the word for show

parts.note: to evince is to show

indicators.note: retiring means going backwards, so the editor's letters are reversed

explanation.surface: An editor on the way out halting a programme to give testimony.
explanation.walkthrough: 'show' is a verb here, to display or reveal, not a television programme.
explanation.definitionFit: Testimony given in court is evidence, a statement offered as proof.

clue.text: Gang get reported over criminal record, making you sort of cross

indicators.note: in a down clue, over sets the first piece above the second
reported tells us the words for gang get are only heard

parts.note: a gang is a crew and to get something is to see it
form is slang for a criminal record

explanation.surface: A gang's report on someone's criminal record leaves you feeling annoyed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cross' looks like angry, but the sense is shaped like a cross.
explanation.definitionFit: Something shaped like a cross is described with this Latin-derived adjective, often of church floor plans.

clue.text: Composer is bloody rattled, repeatedly gutted

indicators.note: both bloody and rattled have their insides removed, keeping first and last letters

explanation.surface: A composer who is thoroughly shaken up, more than once.
explanation.definitionFit: William Byrd was a leading English Renaissance composer of church music.

clue.text: Caricaturist is right to stop BBC with a level of resistance

indicators.note: to stop means to plug something inside the nickname of the BBC

parts.note: the Beeb is a nickname of the British Broadcasting Corporation
the ohm is the unit of electrical resistance

explanation.surface: A cartoonist determined to block the BBC with a show of opposition.
explanation.definitionFit: Max Beerbohm was an English essayist and celebrated caricaturist of Edwardian society.

clue.text: About to leave cohort breaking up ancient footing

indicators.note: breaking up shuffles what remains of cohort
to leave asks for the letter for about to be taken out of cohort

parts.note: C, for circa, means about
ancient means old

explanation.surface: Someone about to quit a group that is splitting, on old ground.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to leave' takes C from cohort, leaving OHORT, which 'breaking up' turns into ROOTH.
explanation.definitionFit: A plant's grip in the soil gives it a firm footing or foothold.

clue.text: Refined woman that can turn either way

indicators.note: a word that can turn either way reads the same forwards and backwards

parts.note: these definition words give the whole answer, and the answer is itself the palindrome: it reads the same from either end

explanation.surface: A genteel lady who can change direction at will.
explanation.definitionFit: The polite form of address to a lady, especially the Queen, suits a refined woman.

clue.text: Record note on UAE currency

indicators.note: in a down clue, on puts the first piece on top of the second

parts.note: a memo is a note
the rial or riyal is a Gulf currency; the Qatar and Dubai riyal was used in the emirates before the dirham

explanation.surface: Writing a note about the money used in the United Arab Emirates.
explanation.definitionFit: A memorial is a written record or chronicle, as well as a monument.

clue.text: Tiny alteration in height, and hence position

indicators.note: a tiny alteration is a change of just one letter in the word for height

parts.note: altitude is height

explanation.surface: A small change in height that alters one's position.
explanation.walkthrough: The tiny change swaps the L of ALTITUDE for a T.
explanation.definitionFit: An aircraft's attitude is its orientation, and more generally an attitude is a posture or position.

clue.text: Green activist told at first to enter confine

indicators.note: to enter puts the initials inside the word for confine

parts.note: to immure is to wall up or confine

indicators.note: at first takes the opening letters of activist and told

explanation.surface: An environmental activist being told to go into lockdown.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Green' suggests the activist, but it is the definition, meaning inexperienced.
explanation.definitionFit: Green means inexperienced or callow, so not yet grown up.

clue.text: I almost trained wild sloth

indicators.note: wild signals the remaining letters running out of order
almost drops the last letter of trained

explanation.surface: A boast about almost taming a wild sloth.
explanation.walkthrough: 'almost' leaves TRAINE, which 'wild' turns into NERTIA. 'sloth' looks like the animal but means laziness.
explanation.definitionFit: Inertia is a reluctance to act or move, a synonym of sloth as idleness.

clue.text: Somewhat hard to stop a type of judge?

indicators.note: to stop means to block a gap within the word for a judge

parts.note: a rater is someone who judges or assesses
H is the abbreviation for hard, as on pencils

explanation.surface: It is fairly difficult to halt a certain kind of judge.
explanation.definitionFit: Rather in the sense of fairly or to some degree is a synonym of somewhat.

clue.text: Sporadic copies I'd revised

indicators.note: revised means reworked, so the letters are put in a new order

explanation.surface: Irregular copies that someone has edited.
explanation.definitionFit: Episodic means occurring in separate episodes, so irregular or occasional.

clue.text: Nothing left by head of organisation that's located in Europe

indicators.note: by means next to, so the head letter follows

parts.note: O is nothing, zero
port is the left side of a ship

indicators.note: head of picks the first letter of organisation

explanation.surface: A firm with nothing left, apart from its boss, based on the Continent.
explanation.definitionFit: Oporto, the English name for Porto, is a city in northern Portugal, on the European mainland.

clue.text: Really into Dutch university by old port (American)

parts.note: the multiplication sign X is read as by, as in three by four
Rio de Janeiro is a Brazilian port

explanation.surface: A Dutch university beside an old port with an American connection.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dutch' looks like the nationality, but 'my old Dutch' is Cockney slang for one's wife.
explanation.definitionFit: Being excessively fond of one's wife, which Cockney slang calls one's Dutch, is the meaning of this word.

clue.text: Faith school dramas unfolding since being rejected

indicators.note: unfolding suggests dramas opening out into a different order
being rejected means sent back, so the word for since reads backwards

parts.note: as means since, because

explanation.surface: Plays staged at a religious school, though they were turned down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unfolding' turns DRAMAS into MADRAS; 'being rejected' turns AS into SA.
explanation.definitionFit: A madrassa is an Islamic school or college, so a religious school.

clue.text: Daughter in a race, initially wearing white coat?

indicators.note: in puts the letter for daughter inside the race

parts.note: the mile is a classic running race

indicators.note: initially takes the first letter of wearing

explanation.surface: A daughter running a race while wearing a lab coat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'white coat' looks like a doctor's garment; the question mark flags the whitish fungal coating.
explanation.definitionFit: Mildew forms a whitish fungal growth over plants and damp surfaces, so it is a white coating.
